title: Psalms Bible Quiz - Chapter 26
description: Ten questions on Psalms 26: a plea to be judged for walking in integrity, washing hands in innocence and loving the house where Yahweh's glory dwells.

questions.text: Why does the psalmist ask Yahweh to judge him in verse 1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:1 says, 'Judge me, Yahweh, for I have walked in my integrity.'

answers.text: He has walked in his integrity

questions.text: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to try?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says, 'Examine me, Yahweh, and prove me. Try my heart and my mind.'

questions.text: What is before the psalmist's eyes?
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:3 says, 'For your loving kindness is before my eyes.'

questions.text: With whom has the psalmist not sat?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says, 'I have not sat with deceitful men, neither will I go in with hypocrites.'

questions.text: What does the psalmist say he hates?
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:5 says, 'I hate the assembly of evildoers.'

questions.text: In what will the psalmist wash his hands?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says, 'I will wash my hands in innocence, so I will go about your altar, Yahweh.'

questions.text: Why will the psalmist go about Yahweh's altar?
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 say he will go about the altar to make the voice of thanksgiving heard and tell of all Yahweh's wondrous deeds.

answers.text: To make the voice of thanksgiving heard
To offer a bull as a burnt offering
To ask Yahweh for riches and honor
To speak with the priests at the gate

questions.text: How does the psalmist describe the house he loves?
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:8 says, 'I love the habitation of your house, the place where your glory dwells.'

answers.text: The place where the kings meet
The place of the evening sacrifice
The place where Yahweh's glory dwells

questions.text: With what is the right hand of the bloodthirsty men full?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says their right hand is full of bribes.

questions.text: Where does the psalmist's foot stand in the last verse?
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:12 says, 'My foot stands in an even place.'
